authority.legal_name: Thames Clippers (London river bus; TfL-coordinated River Bus network)
authority.geography_type: a tidal river (the Thames) running through central London to the estuary, with a tidal flood barrier

mandate.summary: Thames Clippers operates London's principal River Bus network (branded Uber Boat by Thames Clippers), coordinated with Transport for London as part of London's public transport. It runs the RB1/RB2/RB4/RB6 services across 24 piers between Putney in the west and Barking Riverside in the east, carrying millions of commuter and visitor journeys a year.
current_priorities: Run the River Bus network (RB1, RB2, RB4 cross-river, RB6) across 24 piers, integrated with TfL
Deliver the Mayor's Transport Strategy goal of growing river travel and net-zero London by 2030
Decarbonize the fleet - Thames Clippers has introduced the Thames' first hybrid-powered river buses (Earth Clipper, Celestial Clipper) and is moving toward zero-emission operation
Extend river-bus service eastward with new piers (e.g. Barking Riverside) as riverside districts grow

policy_targets.vision: Mayor's Transport Strategy; net-zero-carbon London by 2030; grow the share of trips by river
policy_targets.decarb_note: Thames Clippers has launched the first hybrid-powered river buses on the Thames and is targeting zero-emission operation, aligned with London's 2030 net-zero goal.
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission foiling tier is the fast, low-wake fleet renewal the river bus needs - faster than the current catamarans, near-silent and low-wash for the tidal Thames, advancing London's 2030 net-zero target.

precedent.headline: London already runs a 24-pier commuter River Bus network the length of the tidal Thames.
precedent.network: RB1 (main Battersea/Waterloo-Barking Riverside), RB2 (weekend Embankment-Battersea), RB4 (Canary Wharf-Rotherhithe cross-river), RB6 (Putney-Canary Wharf/North Greenwich) across 24 piers from Putney to Barking Riverside.
precedent.note: The river bus is an established, TfL-coordinated public mode in London. Navier renews and decarbonizes the fleet on the busy central and east-London reaches.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined foiling upgrade to a river-bus network London already runs at commuter scale. Foiling hulls are faster and far lower-wash - important on the wake-restricted tidal Thames - and the speed advantage compounds on the longer east-London reaches toward Canary Wharf, Greenwich, Royal Wharf, Woolwich and Barking Riverside.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/wharves/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public-ferry stops; new/committed stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The core central-to-Docklands commuter reach - Embankment to Canary Wharf; the busiest river-bus demand, foiling-upgraded and low-wash.
Canary Wharf to North Greenwich (The O2) - high-frequency east-London hop.
Battersea Power Station to London Bridge City through the central reaches - fast, near-silent, low-wash.
The full western reach - Putney to Blackfriars (displacement / no-foil through the central bridge spans).
The RB4 cross-river ferry - Canary Wharf to Rotherhithe; short, frequent, wake-sensitive.
East-London growth reach to the new Barking Riverside pier via Royal Wharf and Woolwich.
Woolwich (Royal Arsenal) to Canary Wharf - a fast east-London commuter leg the speed advantage transforms.
Westminster to Greenwich - the classic central-to-maritime-Greenwich run.

regional_links.note: The river bus is a domestic, within-London network on the tidal Thames. There is no cross-border or long-range domestic marine corridor in scope; estuary services beyond the Thames Barrier toward Gravesend/Tilbury are out of the core proposal.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: The Thames Barrier at Woolwich Reach is a moveable flood barrier; eastbound legs to Royal Wharf/Woolwich/Barking Riverside must pass through the marked open navigation spans and obey PLA barrier-closure signals - never route across a closed span.

The Thames is fast-flowing and tidal with PLA wash and speed restrictions through central London; central reaches must be displacement / no-foil and low-wash, with foiling reserved for the wider, clearer east-London reaches where permitted.

Central London has many bridges (Putney, Wandsworth, Battersea, Chelsea, Vauxhall, Lambeth, Westminster, Blackfriars, Southwark, London, Tower); keep geometry in the marked navigation arch of each bridge.
The Thames carries heavy tripboat, freight (tug-and-barge aggregate), and Woolwich Ferry traffic under PLA control; respect navigation rules and cross the Woolwich free-ferry crossing cleanly.
Putney is near the tidal navigation limit; the upper-western reach dries and shoals at low water - route the dredged channel and respect tide windows.
Houseboats and moorings line the central and western reaches with strict no-wash rules; geofence low-wake zones along all moored frontages and pier approaches.
